introHeading: Editorial portraits for Queens' biggest guest lists
introParas: Queens weddings tend to run large — multigenerational catering-hall receptions in Astoria and Flushing that easily clear two or three hundred guests, all of whom made the effort to dress for it. The glam booth handles that scale the same way it handles a smaller party: our own studio lighting rig renders every guest's skin tone evenly regardless of how many have come through before them, and unlimited prints and digital copies mean nobody is turned away because the count ran high.

It is also a natural companion to the mirror booth at bigger Queens events. When a catering hall's guest list is large enough that one line would run all night, pairing the glam booth with a second station or a roaming attendant keeps both moving — worth mentioning when you request your quote if your Forest Hills or Jamaica venue is expecting a crowd. Setup wants 10ft x 10ft for the backdrop and prop table, compressing to 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of clearance for tighter halls, plus a standard 110V outlet within 15 feet.

Long Island City's newer event spaces bring a different flavor — smaller, design-forward parties where the black-and-white look fits a more editorial aesthetic. Wherever the venue sits, from Ridgewood to Flushing, Queens is a standard service area with no surprise travel fees, quoted from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqHeading: Glam Photo Booth in Queens — FAQ

faqs.q: Can the glam booth keep up with a large Astoria or Flushing catering-hall wedding?
faqs.a: Yes — unlimited sessions and unlimited prints mean guest count isn't a limit. For very large weddings we often suggest pairing the glam booth with a roaming attendant or a second station so the line stays short through cocktail hour.

faqs.q: How much space does the glam booth need at a Queens catering hall?
faqs.a: 10ft x 10ft is optimal for the backdrop, prop table and a red-carpet feel; we can compress to 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance for tighter rooms.

faqs.q: Is color available, or is it black-and-white only?
faqs.a: Both — the black-and-white glam edit is the signature look, but the booth can output color, black-and-white, or let each guest choose.

faqs.q: What power do you need at a Forest Hills or Jamaica venue?
faqs.a: A standard 110V, 5-amp, 3-prong outlet within 15 feet of the booth. Most catering halls in this part of Queens have one available near the reception floor.

faqs.q: Do you charge a travel fee to Queens?
faqs.a: No surprise fees. Queens is a standard service area and we quote travel from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqs.q: Is the skin-smoothing retouch too strong, or can we tone it down?
faqs.a: It's fully adjustable — we can push it toward a full editorial look or keep it subtle so guests still look like themselves. Tell us your preference before the event.

faqs.q: Can you send a certificate of insurance for a Queens catering hall that requires one?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $2 million insurance policy — reply to your booking confirmation with the venue's contact and we will send it over.

faqs.q: Is the glam booth a fit for a Long Island City corporate or design-forward event?
faqs.a: Yes — the black-and-white editorial look works especially well at the smaller, design-conscious event spaces that have opened up in LIC in recent years.
